blocks.md: A job moves through a small lifecycle: available, leased, then acknowledged or returned for another attempt. Capacity counts every accepted payload until `Ack`, including work currently held by a worker.

blocks.label: FIG 1
blocks.caption: Nack or visibility expiry returns a leased job to the back of the available queue. It receives a fresh token when leased again.

blocks.title: Leased is still resident
blocks.md: Do not free capacity when a worker leases a job. The queue owns those bytes until `Ack`; otherwise producers can overfill memory while consumers hold leases.

blocks.label: What you implement
blocks.code: func OpenQueue(dir string, capacityBytes uint64) (contract.Queue, error)

blocks.input:
Enqueue A, B
Lease A (deadline 10)
Nack A
Lease ?
blocks.explain: Nack makes A available again at the back. FIFO is defined by availability, so B must be leased before A because it is already waiting.

items: Copy payloads on enqueue and return a unique token for every lease attempt.
Blocked producers and consumers must wake on cancellation or close.
Expired leases return in ascending deadline order, with enqueue order breaking ties.
Ack and Nack reject stale or already-used tokens.

items.title: Write the state machine
items.md: Keep available order, leased records, resident-byte accounting, and token validity explicit.

items.title: Make waiting correct
items.md: Recheck the predicate after every wake; cancellation and close are outcomes, not side notes.

items.title: Then reduce contention
items.md: Replace broadcast wakeups and linear expiry scans only after race tests and lifecycle tests pass.

blocks.title: Why virtual time matters
blocks.md: Lease expiry is driven by the injected `nowTick`, never wall time. The same seed therefore produces the same redeliveries, waits, and score.
